articles.title: India's Sports Ministry Has Sent a 'Sports Passport' Proposal to the PM's Office. For Diaspora Athletes, It Changes Everything.
articles.excerpt: If approved, the framework could let PIO and OCI athletes represent India in international competition without surrendering foreign citizenship — a first in Indian sports history, and a potential game-changer ahead of the 2036 Olympics bid.
articles.image_caption: India's national football team in action during the 2018 SAFF Championship
articles.nri_angle: Millions of Indian-origin athletes who grew up playing football, tennis, and basketball in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia have been legally barred from representing India. The Sports Passport proposal directly addresses the diaspora's exclusion from Indian national teams.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Decades at MIT Press, and Now She Runs Columbia's. Meet Gita Manaktala.
articles.excerpt: Columbia University has appointed the Indian American publishing leader as Executive Director of one of the nation's oldest and most respected university presses — a quiet milestone in a field where South Asian representation at the top remains rare.
articles.image_caption: Columbia University's Morningside Heights campus in New York City
articles.nri_angle: Manaktala's appointment adds to the growing but still thin ranks of Indian Americans leading major American academic and cultural institutions — a quieter form of diaspora achievement than tech CEO headlines, but one that shapes what knowledge gets published, who gets heard, and which ideas reach global audiences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Bay Area Hindu Temples Hit in Weeks. All Five Indian-American Lawmakers Just Demanded Answers.
articles.excerpt: In an unprecedented move, every Indian-American member of Congress has written jointly to the DOJ after a wave of pro-Khalistan vandalism struck temples from Hayward to Newark. The State Department and India's foreign minister have also weighed in.
articles.image_caption: A Hindu temple in California, representative of the community institutions being targeted
articles.nri_angle: Hindu temples in the Bay Area — the heart of the Indian-American tech community — are being systematically targeted, prompting an unprecedented joint response from all five Indian-American members of Congress.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fifty-Six Years After a Prayer at Le Bourget, France Is Getting Its First Traditional Hindu Temple
articles.excerpt: The BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Bussy-Saint-Georges opens in September with a thirteen-day Festival of Culture — a milestone for Europe's Indian diaspora that began with a 1970 airport layover.
articles.image_caption: Carved stone deities at a traditional Hindu temple — the same craft tradition behind the Paris mandir
articles.nri_angle: The Paris mandir fills a gap for hundreds of thousands of Indians across Western Europe who have lacked a traditionally built stone temple, and its September inauguration is already drawing NRI families from the US, UK, and Gulf into pilgrimage-tourism packages.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Singapore Just Blocked Fourteen Posts Targeting Its Indian Community. The Content Likely Came from China.
articles.excerpt: The city-state invoked its Online Criminal Harms Act to order YouTube, Facebook, and X to disable videos claiming Singapore was being 'overrun by Indians' — a rare, swift use of state power to defend diaspora communities.
articles.image_caption: A street in Little India, Singapore, adorned with colourful cultural decorations
articles.nri_angle: Singapore's decisive legal intervention to protect its Indian minority offers a sharp contrast to how other countries with large NRI populations have responded to anti-Indian sentiment — and raises questions about what legal tools are available elsewhere.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven 'Ratnas' and a 57-Year Legacy: Inside the AIA-NY Annual Benefit Gala 2026
articles.excerpt: The oldest Indian-American organisation honoured a xenotransplantation pioneer, a Harvard AI entrepreneur, and five other trailblazers at a packed Flushing gathering — then announced plans for its 39th Deepavali celebration.
articles.image_caption: The Association of Indians in America held its annual gala at Terrace on the Park in Flushing, New York
articles.nri_angle: Oldest Indian-American organisation (founded 1967) honours new generation of NRI achievers; event bridges generational and professional divides in the community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Coming Home to Concrete: How the Gulf War Is Fuelling a Kerala Property Rush Among NRIs
articles.excerpt: Four months of conflict in West Asia have pushed Gulf-based Keralites to hedge their futures with flats and plots back home — even as construction costs surge 35 per cent and builders struggle to keep up.
articles.image_caption: New residential developments in Kochi, Kerala, where NRI property demand has surged amid the West Asia conflict
articles.nri_angle: Gulf-based Keralite NRIs — one of India's largest remittance communities — are reassessing permanent settlement plans; war is accelerating a generational shift from 'earn abroad, retire home' to 'invest now, return sooner.'
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: American India Foundation Raises Record $3.8 Million at 25th Anniversary Gala in New York
articles.excerpt: The milestone evening at Cipriani Wall Street honoured Infosys CEO Salil Parekh, retired TD Bank chief Bharat Masrani and BNY — with over $1 million pledged from the floor in a single night
articles.image_caption: A gala event hall set for a formal philanthropic dinner
articles.nri_angle: AIF's quarter-century record demonstrates the maturing financial muscle of Indian-American philanthropy — channelling diaspora wealth back into education, health and livelihoods across 35 Indian states and union territories.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UAE Arrests 19 Indian Nationals for Spreading Fake Missile Videos Amid Gulf Tensions
articles.excerpt: As the Iran-US conflict enters its fourth month, Dubai authorities crack down on misinformation — and the diaspora's largest Gulf community finds itself caught in the crossfire
articles.image_caption: The Dubai skyline — home to the UAE's largest concentration of Indian expatriates
articles.nri_angle: With 3.5 million Indians in the UAE — the single largest expatriate community in any Gulf state — the arrests are a sharp reminder of how wartime information laws can ensnare diaspora workers unfamiliar with local legal thresholds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Teen Gurnoor Kaur Wins Canada's National Data Science Contest With AI Wheat-Disease Model
articles.excerpt: The Grade 11 student from Ontario built a predictive system that forecasts climate-driven crop pathogen outbreaks — and took home a $1,200 Scale AI prize
articles.image_caption: A golden wheat field — the crop at the centre of Kaur's AI disease-prediction model
articles.nri_angle: Kaur's win adds to a growing roster of Indian-origin students excelling in North American STEM competitions — part of a second-generation pattern where children of immigrants leverage parental emphasis on education into nationally recognised research.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Let Me Cook and Feed People': An Indian Woman's Response to Belfast's Anti-Immigrant Violence
articles.excerpt: As masked mobs torched homes in Northern Ireland, Ruchira Rangaprasad rallied 30 strangers to deliver food to terrified families
articles.image_caption: Volunteers distributing packaged food at a community relief drive
articles.nri_angle: Indian immigrant in Northern Ireland leads grassroots food relief amid anti-immigrant riots, symbolising cross-community solidarity within the diaspora
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Wait Gets Longer: EB-2 India Retrogression Rattles Thousands of NRI Professionals
articles.excerpt: The June 2026 Visa Bulletin pushed back priority dates for Indian applicants, adding fresh uncertainty to careers, mortgages, and family plans
articles.image_caption: Indian-born professionals across America face renewed uncertainty after the June 2026 Visa Bulletin
articles.nri_angle: Green card backlog directly impacts NRI professionals' career mobility, home ownership, and long-term family planning in America
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Temple Weddings to Pickleball Courts: TANA Is Rewriting the Telugu Diaspora Playbook
articles.excerpt: A grand Kalyanam in New York and a 65-team pickleball tournament in North Carolina show how America's Telugu community is building year-round institutional infrastructure.
articles.image_caption: Indian community cultural celebrations — TANA is expanding its programming from conferences to year-round events across America
articles.nri_angle: TANA's expansion from biennial conferences to year-round events — spiritual, recreational, professional — mirrors the Telugu diaspora's growth into one of America's fastest-expanding Indian language communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Indian American Lawmakers Are at the Centre of America's State-Level Fight Over ICE
articles.excerpt: Nikil Saval in Pennsylvania and Ravinder Bhalla in New Jersey are drafting legislation to limit federal immigration enforcement in state institutions — placing diaspora politicians at the sharp end of the debate.
articles.image_caption: Indian American lawmakers are increasingly shaping state-level policy on immigration enforcement
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans in state legislatures have roughly doubled since 2018. Saval and Bhalla's immigration bills show the diaspora moving from federal visibility to state-level policy influence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Museum for Thirty Million People: GOPIO's Plan for the World's First Indian Diaspora Institution
articles.excerpt: The Global Organisation of People of Indian Origin wants to build a permanent museum in New Delhi with four galleries tracing Indian migration from indenture to the tech boom. The Hinduja Foundation has pledged its support.
articles.image_caption: Indian heritage artefacts — GOPIO envisions four permanent galleries tracing the diaspora's journey from indenture to the technology age
articles.nri_angle: A Delhi-based museum would be the first institution to curate the full arc of Indian emigration — from colonial indenture to the American tech diaspora — and could serve as a hub for scattered community archives worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Telangana MBA Student Took a Pizza Delivery Shift. He Was Lured to a Vacant Apartment and Shot Dead.
articles.excerpt: Anshul Kuncha, 28, was found with a gunshot wound to the head outside a Philadelphia housing complex. Police say the order was placed for an empty unit. No arrests have been made.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of Philadelphia, where Anshul Kuncha was fatally shot during a pizza delivery
articles.nri_angle: An Indian MBA student working part-time delivery to fund US education was killed in a suspected trap order. Highlights the dangerous reality facing 300,000+ Indian students who work gig jobs in America. Indian Consulate in New York has confirmed his identity and offered condolences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian Seafarers Are Missing After a U.S. Military Strike on a Tanker Off Oman. India Has Summoned the American Envoy.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi lodged a 'strong protest' after precision munitions hit the Settebello in the Gulf of Oman, leaving 21 Indian crew rescued and three unaccounted for.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea — Indian mariners crew a disproportionate share of the world's commercial fleet
articles.nri_angle: India supplies roughly 240,000 of the world's 1.9 million commercial seafarers. The blockade risks NRI lives in the Gulf's volatile shipping lanes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Made It Easier for NRIs to Own Bigger Stakes in Indian Companies. Here Is What Changed.
articles.excerpt: Individual investment caps for NRIs and OCIs in listed Indian equities have already doubled to 10 per cent this year. The central bank says it will push them higher.
articles.image_caption: Stock market data on a financial trading screen
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors in the US, UK and Gulf can now build larger positions in Indian stocks without the regulatory burden of SEBI's FPI registration route.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bihar Wants Its Global Diaspora to Help Build the State. It Just Launched a Portal to Make That Possible.
articles.excerpt: A new digital platform invites overseas Biharis to pitch ideas, volunteer expertise and propose investments directly to the state government.
articles.image_caption: An aerial view of the Gandhi Setu bridge spanning the Ganges River in Patna, Bihar
articles.nri_angle: Bihar produces some of India's sharpest minds for the global workforce but has struggled to channel diaspora expertise back into state development.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: They Had Careers, a Flat in Clapham, and a Son Who Could Not Speak. On the Morning of 27 May, All Three Fell from the 36th Floor.
articles.excerpt: The deaths of Rakesh Pai, Aditi Paralkar, and their nine-year-old son Sid in a London tower block have forced a reckoning with the mental health crisis hiding in plain sight across the Indian diaspora.
articles.image_caption: The Elephant and Castle skyline in south London, where the Pai-Paralkar family lived in the Highpoint tower block
articles.nri_angle: The Pai-Paralkar tragedy exposes the invisible mental health crisis among NRI families: the absence of extended family support, the stigma around seeking help, and the grinding isolation of caregiving for a severely disabled child thousands of miles from home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Poet Just Won America's Top South Asian Translation Prize. The Novel He Translated Changed Nepali Literature Forever.
articles.excerpt: Rohan Chhetri's English rendering of Parijat's 1964 masterpiece Shirishko Phool has won the 2026 Armory Square Prize, bridging one of the diaspora's most enduring literary blind spots.
articles.image_caption: Parijat, the Nepali writer whose 1964 novel Shirishko Phool is the subject of Chhetri's prize-winning translation
articles.nri_angle: Chhetri's career — born in West Bengal, educated in Mumbai and Syracuse, teaching in Cleveland — embodies the transnational literary life the diaspora makes possible. His translation brings one of South Asia's most important novels to a new generation of English-speaking diaspora readers who may have heard the title but never read the book.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven Indian Workers Killed in Dubai After Minibus Rams Into Stalled Truck on Emirates Road.
articles.excerpt: The Indian Consulate is assisting families of the dead and nine others injured in the crash, one of the deadliest road accidents involving Indian nationals in the Gulf this year.
articles.image_caption: Emirates Road in Dubai, where a minibus collided with a stalled truck on Monday killing seven Indian workers
articles.nri_angle: Seven Indian blue-collar workers killed in Dubai road crash; Indian Consulate assisting with repatriation and family support; highlights persistent safety risks for 3.4 million Indians in the UAE.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ninety-Six Unicorns and Counting. Indian Immigrants Are Building More Billion-Dollar Startups Than Any Other Group in America.
articles.excerpt: A new report from the National Foundation for American Policy finds that Indian-born entrepreneurs have founded or co-founded 96 privately held unicorn companies in the United States — more than Israel, Britain, and China combined.
articles.image_caption: Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, the heart of American venture capital where Indian-founded startups have raised billions
articles.nri_angle: Indian immigrants' dominance of American startup culture reflects decades of diaspora entrepreneurship and the compounding effects of networks built by generations of NRIs in Silicon Valley and beyond.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From the Lincoln Memorial to Times Square, India Is Turning America's Most Famous Landmarks Into Yoga Studios
articles.excerpt: The Indian Embassy and consulate will host the 12th International Day of Yoga at two of Washington and New York's most iconic sites, with PM Modi's personal yoga guru headlining the celebrations.
articles.image_caption: International Day of Yoga celebrations with participants practicing outdoors
articles.nri_angle: The annual Yoga Day celebrations have become the Indian diaspora's most visible cultural export — a soft power projection that diaspora organizations have spent a decade building through diplomatic partnerships and community organizing across American cities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 28-Year-Old From Telangana Was Delivering Pizzas in Philadelphia. He Never Made It Back to His Car.
articles.excerpt: Kuncha Anshul was shot dead by masked assailants while completing a late-night delivery order in North Philadelphia. His family in Medchal is now fighting to bring his body home.
articles.image_caption: The Philadelphia skyline — Kuncha Anshul, a 28-year-old from Telangana, was killed while delivering food in the city
articles.nri_angle: The killing adds to a pattern of violence against young Indian workers in the United States who take on gig and delivery jobs to supplement their income — exposing them to the dangers of American urban gun violence that few are prepared for when they arrive.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Just Became India's Longest-Serving Elected PM. The Diaspora's Response Says Everything.
articles.excerpt: US senators, Silicon Valley CEOs, and Indian American community leaders rushed to congratulate the prime minister as he crossed 4,399 consecutive days in office — surpassing Nehru's record.
articles.image_caption: Official portrait of Prime Minister Narendra Modi
articles.nri_angle: The speed and warmth of the diaspora's response — from Capitol Hill to Cupertino — reveals how deeply Modi's tenure has reshaped the Indian American community's political identity and its relationship with New Delhi.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Bay Area Hindu Temples Hit in Weeks. A Pattern Is Forming.
articles.excerpt: Pro-Khalistan graffiti, a theft, and broken windows — the wave of vandalism targeting Hindu worship spaces in Northern California has the community demanding answers and installing cameras.
articles.image_caption: Akshardham Hindu Temple in Jersey City, one of many diaspora worship spaces facing security concerns
articles.nri_angle: For Indian Americans in the Bay Area — home to one of the densest concentrations of Hindu temples in the US — the attacks strike at the heart of community life, turning Sunday worship into a security calculation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Just Hiked NRI Deposit Rates by 300 Basis Points. Here's Why Your Dollar Suddenly Matters More.
articles.excerpt: The RBI is absorbing hedging costs on foreign currency deposits for the first time since 2013. Banks are expected to hoover up $35–40 billion from the diaspora by September.
articles.image_caption: Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata, headquarters of the central bank's eastern operations
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who have parked dollars in low-yield savings accounts abroad, the RBI's move creates a rare arbitrage window — higher returns than US Treasuries, with the central bank eating the currency risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Twenty-One Years and a Ton of Tamil Granite Later, Berlin Has One of Europe's Largest Hindu Temples
articles.excerpt: The Sri Ganesha Temple in Neukölln, funded entirely by donations and seva, opened its doors on June 7 after two decades of construction — a milestone for Germany's fastest-growing diaspora.
articles.image_caption: The Sri Ganesha Hindu Temple in Berlin's Neukölln district on its consecration day, 7 June 2026
articles.nri_angle: Germany's Indian population has surged 70% since 2020 to 260,000, and the Sri Ganesha Temple — built entirely by the Tamil diaspora through donations and voluntary labour — is the most visible symbol yet that the community has moved from survival to permanence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lagaan Turns Twenty-Five, the Goodness Gracious Me Gang Reunites, and London's Indian Film Festival Has Never Been Bigger
articles.excerpt: The 17th edition of Europe's largest South Asian film festival spans five UK cities, brings Aamir Khan to BFI Southbank, and launches the continent's first Indian AI film showcase.
articles.image_caption: Aamir Khan, whose In Conversation session closes the London Indian Film Festival 2026
articles.nri_angle: For 1.8 million British Indians, LIFF is the rare festival that takes South Asian cinema as seriously as any national cinema — and the 2026 edition, with its Lagaan anniversary, Goodness Gracious Me reunion, and AI showcase, captures a diaspora confident enough to celebrate its past and invest in its future.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Bellevue to Brooklyn, Indian Restaurants Are Opening at a Pace America Has Never Seen
articles.excerpt: A Michelin-recognised bistro chain, a $2-billion food-hall empire, and a trio of childhood friends with a DC fast-casual — the race to make Indian food mainstream in America is suddenly very crowded.
articles.image_caption: An assortment of Indian dishes including curries, naan, and biryani — the kind of spread Americans are increasingly seeking out
articles.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora built the customer base, the talent pipeline, and the cultural familiarity that now allows Indian cuisine to scale in mainstream American food culture — from fine dining to fast-casual to ghost kitchens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Counting Its People — and Their Caste — for the First Time in 95 Years. Every NRI Should Be Paying Attention.
articles.excerpt: The 2027 Census will reshape parliamentary seats, reservation quotas, and welfare targeting. For a diaspora rooted in the south, the numbers could rearrange everything they thought was settled.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi fills out the self-enumeration form for Census 2027, the first census to go fully digital
articles.nri_angle: Most NRIs originate from southern states that fear losing Lok Sabha seats in delimitation. The census will also shape reservation policy, property rights, and welfare — all areas where NRIs maintain deep personal and financial stakes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
